intervals.note: The carpet installation was completed in June 2006; the guard ring was completed in spring 2007 and connected to the DAQ in November 2007 (Montini et al., arXiv:1608.01251). Start of construction is not stated in the sources read.
intervals.quote: The ARGO-YBJ experiment started recording data with the whole central carpet in June 2006. The period until autumn 2007 has been mainly devoted to installation and debugging operations

physics_goals.quote: The aim of the ARGO-YBJ experiment is to study cosmic rays, mainly cosmic gamma-radiation, at an energy threshold of ~100 GeV
physics_goals.value: Study cosmic rays, mainly cosmic gamma radiation, at an energy threshold of about 100 GeV.

summary.plain: ARGO-YBJ covered a 6700 square metre floor on the Tibetan plateau with a single layer of particle counters to catch even small air showers. It watched the northern sky for TeV gamma rays and studied cosmic rays from 2007 to 2013.
summary.technical: Italian-Chinese full-coverage air-shower array of resistive plate chambers (about 74 × 78 m2 carpet, 18,480 pads) at 4300 m, threshold about 100 GeV; stable data taking November 2007 to February 2013. Results include a five-year Crab Nebula spectrum (21.1 sigma), the p+He spectrum and the cosmic-ray anisotropy.
